title: Uniform supported perfect approximation on an algebraic space
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $Y$ an algebraic space over $S$, with its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_Y$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A strictly perfect complex is bounded with each term a direct summand of a finite free structure module [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]; a perfect object is locally isomorphic to one in the derived category. For $b\in\mathbf Z$, an object $F$ is $b$-pseudo-coherent if, locally on every object of the small etale site, it receives a map from a strictly perfect complex inducing isomorphisms on $H^i$ for $i>b$ and a surjection on $H^b$. Define $\mathsf A(Y)$ as follows. Let $|Y|$ be the point space of $Y$ [def-a1-space-point-topology]; for a closed subset $T\subseteq|Y|$ write $Y\setminus T\subseteq Y$ for the open subspace with point space $|Y|\setminus T$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace], which exists and is unique because open subspaces of $Y$ correspond bijectively to open subsets of $|Y|$ [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], and say that a sheaf of modules $G$ vanishes outside $T$ if its restriction to the small etale site of $Y\setminus T$ is zero. For every closed subset $T\subseteq |Y|$ such that the open immersion $Y\setminus T\to Y$ is quasi-compact (its inverse image under every affine scheme chart is quasi-compact), there is an integer $r$ such that for every $m\in\mathbf Z$ and every $F\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ which is $(m-r)$-pseudo-coherent and such that $H^i(F)$ vanishes outside $T$ for every $i\ge m-r$, there are a perfect $P\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ and a map $v:P\to F$ such that $H^i(P)$ vanishes outside $T$ for every $i$, $H^i(v)$ is an isomorphism for $i>m$, and $H^m(v)$ is surjective. The integer $r$ may depend on $Y,T$, but not on $m,F$.
